speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether more graduated or proportional arrangements for foreign manpower and levy thresholds can be considered for hawkers and small food and beverage operators to meet their essential kitchen and service staffing needs while still ensuring fair wages and protections for all workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: As a unique combination of food, space and community, hawker centres are a microcosm of Singapore’s multicultural society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Stallholders can also hire eligible Long-Term Visit Pass and Long-Term Visit Pass-Plus holders, who are already in Singapore and can contribute to our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: To address the manpower needs of micro enterprises, we allow those with only one local worker to hire their first Work Permit Holder.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This could result in a large increase in the number of foreign workers, which would not be sustainable given our limited infrastructural and social carrying capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: I think if the Member has been reading The Straits Times, she would probably have noticed that there was an opinion piece on 24 February, Tuesday, last week, written by Assoc Prof Lee Kuan-Huei.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: She is the Chief Research Officer of the Singapore Productivity Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In that article, I think there was quite a good data-based opinion of the current state of play in the F&B sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: If I may just share some of the insights from that particular opinion piece.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: She said that there is a structural problem in the way F&B operators here still operate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: One of the key thing is that productivity gains have lagged behind activity growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: That means that the F&B operators are putting more effort and resources into their operations without the proportionate economic gains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: And her suggestion is that productivity and not headcount must be the central lens through which productivity must be assessed and for which business viability has to be looked at.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Companies may also tap on broader schemes such as the Productivity Solutions Grant to support transformation efforts to raise productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We will continue to review the foreign manpower policies for hawkers and small F&B companies, together with relevant agencies, including MSE.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I am also very happy to hear that the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) will continue to review that.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I agree with the writer that structurally, there are some challenges, and productivity is important.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But here, we are looking at the hawkers and the single F&B operators.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: They do not have that advantage of scale to be able to take advantage of the Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) tier.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Therefore, even if they hired just one additional worker, it brings them up to the higher DRC level, if they are even eligible to hire that.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: From the way hawkers and these small, single F&Bs operate, honestly, they are working 12 to 14 hours, and many of the owner operators are working those hours.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: My residents are some of them – that is the reason why I am asking this question.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I do hope the Ministry will look at the data of companies, the single operators and hawkers, that are pushed into this higher tier or end up not even deciding to carry on with their business because it is just getting too hard.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I agree with her that it is a challenge for smaller scale operators.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But this goes beyond just giving more headcount.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It fundamentally revolves around a few key issues.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One is the operating model itself, whether it is sustainable.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is a question that goes beyond policy, because Singaporeans have certain expectations about the quality of the food from the hawkers, the authenticity of the recipe and whether it still tastes like the good old days that they are used to.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In essence, actually, MOM is agnostic to this.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: You see this a lot in food courts, where your typical traditional dish is cooked by a foreign worker.
